crime_highlights: Ms. Saunders had the prohibited firearm in her possession inside her residence
she discharged the prohibited firearm, shooting Laura Taylor in the abdomen.
Ms. Taylor was admitted to hospital and underwent surgery for her injuries.
She continues to require medical care as a result of her injuries.
rationale_highlights: the unique circumstances of Indigenous offenders can diminish the degree of moral blameworthiness for an offence
Ms. Saunders' circumstances, as set out in the Gladue report, do, in my view, diminish her degree of moral blameworthiness for this offence
her mother and other family members being residential school survivors

crime_highlights: The search of Unit 118 yielded substances containing: fentanyl, totalling 111.76 grams; fentanyl and carfentanil totalling 21.22 grams; and methamphetamine totalling 111.04 grams.
Much of it had been weighed and packaged into one-quarter or one-half-ounce dime bags and labelled as such.
At trial, Mr. Kazakoff admitted to being in possession of the seized drugs, but maintained they were for his personal use.
The RCMP also seized $5,000 in Canadian cash in five rolls of $1,000 bills each found in a black jacket that belonged to Mr. Kazakoff.
rationale_highlights: I am not persuaded that Mr. Kazakoff can be fairly characterized as an Indigenous person that would attract the full application of Gladue
the effects of intergenerational trauma could contribute to understanding his experience as a youth and as a teenager
I take into serious consideration Mr. Kazakoff's history
note: Court denies full Gladue; weighs history as substantial mitigating factor (paras 49, 72).
